thread:
rohan: Thinking out loud — proposal for a "soft diversion" rollout guard. Instead of an immediate autopause on cost/latency breaches, we divert a percentage of traffic to a cheaper/stable fallback model and continue telemetry for X minutes before deciding to pause. Keeps UX smoother for customers.

kim: sounds promising. what's the trigger logic? windowed median?

rohan: yeah, I was thinking: two metrics — p95 latency and token_cost_rate (tokens/sec normalized by tenant quota). If p95 > SLO_thresh OR token_cost_rate > cost_thresh for >= 3 consecutive 1m windows, then flip diversion.

ashley: +1 to windowing. also add a dampening factor so noisy tenants don't flip us constantly. maybe require at least N requests or a min tokens sample.

dave: curious about failure modes — if fallback model has lower quality, we need to surface a clear signal in Console (banner + explanation) and tag the rollback reason in traces.

rohan: agreed. Console UX idea: when diversion active show yellow banner "Traffic partially diverted to fallback due to latency or cost guard" with links to: trace view, recent prompts sample, and option to "force pause".

kim: how do we implement diversion? at routing layer or via config to the canary? My vote: routing layer so we can do perc-based diversion without changing canary config.

rohan: routing layer makes sense. pseudo-config idea:
```
rollout_guards:
  - name: soft_diversion_v1
    triggers:
      - metric: p95_latency_ms
        op: ">"
        threshold: 1200
        windows: 3
      - metric: token_cost_rate
        op: ">"
        threshold: 0.75
        windows: 3
    action: divert
    divert_policy:
      percent: 30
      fallback_model: rwd-base-1
      evaluation_window: 10m

```

ashley: neat. what about escalation? if after eval_window the metrics don't improve, we auto-pause?

rohan: yes — state machine: normal -> diverted -> paused. After diverted, if metrics still > threshold for 2 eval windows then auto-pause; if metrics drop below a lower recovery_threshold for 2 windows we return to normal and gradually ramp traffic back.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: canary_id=cr-2026-03-19-52, target=50%

dave: small nit: ensure tenant-scoped thresholds. Multi-tenant big customers will have different baselines. Also supporting per-route overrides for embeddings vs generation because cost patterns differ.

kim: telemetry: we need a composite alert that tracks both absolute and relative cost impact. e.g., absolute extra_tokens/sec and relative pct_increase vs baseline. Without that ops will get noisy alerts.

rohan: agree. I'll sketch an implementation plan: 1) routing layer diversion primitives 2) guard evaluator service with sliding windows 3) Console banners + rollout controls 4) per-tenant threshold config + defaults 5) add canary metadata to traces.

ashley: timeline? can we aim for an MVP that just diverts and shows a banner (no auto-pause) in 3 sprints?

rohan: realistic — MVP = diversion + console signal + basic metrics. Auto-pause and recovery ramp in follow-up. I'll open a PR with config schema and a design doc.

kim: please @dave on the PR for UX review and @ashley for guard tuning.

rohan: done. thanks all :thumbsup:
